cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Try It First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Turn the kitchen tap on before I start washing up. I've tightened the loose joint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Wear my apron. I need to know whether the joint holds.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You wear it and turn the tap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll need it dry for washing up. You can have my raincoat for the test.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 claim decision power, but A5 clothing offer does not distinctly maintain approval over B testing role.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 prior spray causes A3 apron offer; B4 reverses the request and A5 protects the apron with a raincoat substitute, after unrelated restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 remembers a real failed test and B4 asks A to bear it, plausibly resisting unequal exposure.

heightening.evidence: B4 attempted role reversal causes A5 a more protective offer that still keeps B testing first.

specificity.evidence: A1 tightened tap joint before washing up establishes uncertain fix and intended later reliance.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 dry-apron rationale is earned by B4 reversal, while the A3 stock authority sentence is cumbersome.

coach2.inferred: A5 offers protective clothing as persuasion, not proof of repair quality.
coach2.missing: No plumbing diagnosis beyond the stated loose joint is needed.
coach2.firstDefect: A3 generic question restriction does not shape the offered protection specifically.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 protection offer causes B4 to assign apron and test back to A.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 reversal causes A5 a raincoat concession that keeps A apron dry.
